subject: DPA clarifications & data handling follow-up (Acme Payments)
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme-payments.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: DPA clarifications / data handling questions

Thanks again for the call earlier — this was helpful. As discussed, legal and procurement had a few specific follow-ups on the DPA and our data handling requirements. I attached our redlines (Acme_DPA_redlines.pdf) — please see questions inline but I pulled the major asks into bullets below so we can track next steps.

Summary of asks (high-level):
- Confirm roles: will Redwood be the Data Processor and Acme the Data Controller for data we send to the API?
- Subprocessors: need current list and a commitment to notify us of additions. Can you provide a CSV/registry?
- Breach notice: Acme prefers 48 hours for initial notification. Is that negotiable?
- Data residency: we need assurance that production data from our US customers remains in US regions only. What controls do you offer?
- Retention & deletion: we need the ability to request deletion of PII and a window for logs/trace retention (we prefer <=30 days).
- Logging/auditing: what logging controls are available (sampling, redaction, ability to opt out of logging on a per-route basis)?

Next steps we need from Redwood: written answers to the bullets above, your standard DPA (or a redline back), SOC 2 report, and any subprocessor registry. Procurement is aiming to complete legal review by 2026-10-15, so a quick turnaround would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Acme Payments

Attachment: Acme_DPA_redlines.pdf (summary redlines)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme-payments.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications / data handling questions

Hi Alicia — great to meet earlier, and thanks for the clear summary + redlines. I've pulled together initial answers below and attached a couple of items (Redwood_SOC2_report_2026.pdf, subprocessor-list.csv). Marissa (CS) is looped in and can coordinate procurement/legal where needed.

Quick answers (high-level):
- Roles: Redwood acts as a Data Processor; customers are Controllers for data they send. We process requests to provide inference and related services (we do not claim controller status for customer-provided content).
- Subprocessors: attached is our current registry (subprocessor-list.csv). We notify customers of material subprocessor changes via the admin console and email — standard notification window is 30 days, expedited for security-critical changes.
- Breach notice: our target is to provide initial notification within 72 hours of confirming an incident, with follow-ups as material facts are discovered. We'll include interim updates; committing to 48 hours in all cases is operationally difficult but we can escalate to Legal for negotiation on high-risk accounts.
- Data residency: we support region pinning for production workloads (US, EU). For Acme, we can pin inference and persistent storage to US regions and restrict backups to US as well. I included details below on options.
- Retention & deletion: default request/response logs are retained 30 days, with the option for customers on Dedicated/Private deployments to set custom retention (including deletion at request). For hosted accounts we can offer a 30-day retention SLA and support targeted deletion requests; we can discuss an auditable deletion confirmation.
- Logging/auditing: we provide token-level cost/latency logging, configurable sampling, and an opt-out for logging on specific routes (subject to agreement where logs are needed for abuse detection). Detailed control is part of our Console features.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_report_2026.pdf, subprocessor-list.csv. I also attached our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_standard_v2.pdf) in the follow-up email — forwarding that now to make it easy for legal to review.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa to send standard DPA to Acme (with link/attachment).
2) If Acme has redlines, Ben/Marissa will route to Legal for a focused review; we aim to respond within 3 business days for routine redlines.
3) If breach-notice timing or specific deletion language is a blocker, we can escalate to our Legal lead for a call with Acme Legal.

Would you like to schedule a quick call with Legal this week?

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments in this message: Redwood_SOC2_report_2026.pdf, subprocessor-list.csv

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme-payments.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications / data handling questions

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from our side after reviewing the SOC2 and your notes:

- Controller/Processor: confirming that wording in the DPA explicitly states Redwood is the Processor and Acme is Controller. Our legal wants the clause verbatim (can you highlight the relevant section in the DPA PDF?).
- Breach notice: 48 hours is Acme's preference. If you cannot commit contractually to 48 hours, we need a clear escalation path and an SLA-like commitment to timely updates (timestamped). Please confirm whether Redwood can add a contractual clause for 'initial notification within 72 hours with good-faith updates every 48 hours thereafter until resolution' — that would be acceptable to us.
- Deletion: we need an auditable deletion certificate (timestamped confirmation of deletion of requested PII) with scope (API logs, model-cache, backups). Is that something Redwood can provide on a per-request basis?
- Subprocessors: can Redwood include a right to audit subprocessors or at least require written notice + opportunity to object to materially new subprocessors that will process Acme data?

Procurement timeline reminder: we are targeting 2026-10-15 for execution. If possible, please send the native DPA (fillable PDF or DocuSign link).

Thanks — Alicia

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@acme-payments.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications / data handling questions

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear follow-up and the timeline. I've attached our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_standard_v2.pdf) and a redlined response (redlined_DPA_response.pdf) that highlights the processor/controller language and the sections that address subprocessors, breach notification, and deletion. Quick answers to your asks below and next steps.

- Controller/Processor: Section 2.1 in the attached DPA explicitly names Acme as Controller and Redwood as Processor; I've highlighted that clause in redlined_DPA_response.pdf for easy reference.
- Breach notice: Our standard contractual commitment is initial notification within 72 hours after confirmation of an incident, with timely follow-ups. Your proposed phrasing ('initial notification within 72 hours with good-faith updates every 48 hours thereafter') is reasonable — we can present that to Legal. We can't unilaterally change all customers' SLAs, but for enterprise deals we can include that as a negotiated addendum.

- Deletion & certificate: For hosted accounts we offer deletion on request with a confirmation report; for Dedicated/Private customers we can provide auditable deletion logs and an export showing deletion timestamps. We can include language in the DPA to confirm Redwood will provide a deletion confirmation on request.
- Subprocessors & audit: We cannot provide unrestricted on-site audits of third-party subprocessors, but we do offer: 1) a maintained subprocessor registry with 30-day notice for additions, 2) the right to review SOC/ISO reports for new subprocessors upon request, and 3) an objection process for materially new subprocessors (we'll escalate objections to Legal). We documented this in the redline.

Next steps:
1) Please review redlined_DPA_response.pdf and confirm which clauses are blockers.
2) If acceptable, I'll send the native DocuSign link for signature (https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/D-2026-ACME-42).
3) If Acme Legal requests changes beyond the redline, we'll route to our Legal team and aim for a turnaround within 3 business days; for high-risk deviations we'll set up a short legal-to-legal call.

I've attached: Redwood_DPA_standard_v2.pdf, redlined_DPA_response.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_report_2026.pdf. Let me know if you'd like to set a time today for a brief legal call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_standard_v2.pdf, redlined_DPA_response.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_report_2026.pdf
